verses.text: Paul, a prisoner for Christ Jesus, and our brother Timothy, to Philemon, our dear co-worker,
to our dear sister Apphia, to Archippus, our fellow soldier, and to the church that meets in your home:
Grace and peace to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
I always thank my God when I remember you in my prayers,
because I've heard about your love and faith in the Lord Jesus and toward all God's people.
I pray that sharing your faith will help you recognize every good thing we have in Christ.
Your love has brought me great joy and encouragement, because you, brother, have refreshed the hearts of God's people.
So even though I have every right in Christ to tell you what you should do,
I'd rather appeal to you on the basis of love. I, Paul, am an old man now, and I'm also a prisoner for Christ Jesus.
I'm appealing to you for my child Onesimus, whose spiritual father I became while in chains.
Once he was useless to you, but now he's useful both to you and to me.
I'm sending him back to you—and with him, my own heart.
I would have liked to keep him with me so he could serve me on your behalf while I'm in chains for the Good News.
But I didn't want to do anything without your consent, so your kindness would come from choice, not obligation.
Perhaps he was separated from you for a while so you could have him back forever—
no longer as an enslaved person, but as more than that: a dearly loved brother. He's especially dear to me, and even more to you, both as a person and as a brother in the Lord.
So if you consider me a partner, welcome him as you would welcome me.
If he has wronged you in any way or owes you anything, charge it to me.
I, Paul, am writing this with my own hand: I'll repay it. (I won't mention that you owe me your very self.)
Yes, brother, let me have this joy from you in the Lord. Refresh my heart in Christ.
I'm confident you'll obey. I'm writing because I know you'll do even more than I'm asking.
One more thing: prepare a guest room for me, because I hope your prayers will bring me back to you.
Epaphras, my fellow prisoner in Christ Jesus, sends greetings.
So do Mark, Aristarchus, Demas, and Luke, my co-workers.
May the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit. Amen.
